※ This passage lacks sources; still to be verified: The kamaycha is a traditional string instrument of the Crimean Tatars, originating in Crimea in Central Asia; its name means 'bent' or 'bow-shaped', which reflects the distinctive curved design of the body. The instrument sounds with a bow, and its timbre is bright and exciting, with a metallic quality and strong carrying power, its range lying in the upper middle register. The design of its resonating cavity projects the sound forcefully outwards, so it stands out clearly in a folk ensemble. The kamaycha combines traditional character with a modern sound quality, and suits warm, uninhibited, passionate music.
